title: Sageuk Ink — Joseon Opening Title
description: A cinematic reinterpretation of the sageuk drama title card: sumi-ink ground, one dancheong-colored horizontal band in vermillion and azurite, and a vertically-set heavy Myeongjo headline with Hanja episode notation at small scale.
philosophy: This template exists to honor the precise visual grammar of Joseon-era ceremony — the tension between deep ink silence and the sudden shock of dancheong pigment. It refuses horizontal Roman type conventions and gradient backgrounds, insisting on vertical script, painted brushstroke texture, and the architectural restraint of a single chromatic band. It is built for speakers who understand that gravitas is earned through subtraction, not addition. The audience it serves does not need decoration; it needs the weight of dynasty.
goodFor: Drama series or documentary chapter-title slides
Korean cultural heritage and traditional-arts presentations
Period-themed event programs or ceremony runsheets
Single-statement title cards demanding maximum visual gravity
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews or data dashboards
Multi-column layouts requiring dense Roman-script body copy
Casual consumer lifestyle or startup pitch contexts
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a cinematographer's first frame of a dynasty epic — oppressive sumi-ink silence broken by one raw horizontal stripe of dancheong pigment, vivid as lacquered ceremonial wood lit by a single torch. Compositional rhythm is vertical and unhurried: the headline descends like an inscription chiseled into a palace stele, carrying no urgency, only authority. The chromatic band functions architecturally, not decoratively — a controlled shock, not an ornament. Avoid any gradient, centered bilateral symmetry, or modern digital gloss; the mood must register as ceremony, not design.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed ink-ground canvas with no outer margin band — brushstroke texture runs edge to edge on all four sides. A single full-width horizontal chromatic band occupies the lower third of the slide, serving as the sole structural divider and the only source of concentrated color. The vertically-oriented headline is set in the upper-right quadrant of a loose eight-column grid, reading top-to-bottom in the traditional East Asian axis, with generous ink field to its left acting as negative-space counterweight. Hanja episode notation sits at diminutive scale in the bottom-left corner, isolated from the headline by the vast silence of the ink ground.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a held breath between scenes — a ceremonial inscription, not delivered information. Asymmetric composition: a deep ink void on the left holds a brushstroke motif, while the right column carries content text with upright, unhurried authority. The dancheong band bisects the field as a sudden chromatic caesura — never decorative, always structural. Avoid horizontal copy blocks, bullet clusters, or any lightness that would betray the dynastic gravity of the ink ground.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with full-bleed sumi-ink ground; a single dancheong horizontal band of roughly one-tenth slide height anchors the vertical midpoint, acting as the lone chromatic spine. Primary content — a single distilled statement or attributed quote rendered in vertically-oriented script — occupies cols 7–11, with the generous left void (cols 1–5) given over to a brushstroke texture or ink-wash motif that bleeds from the left edge. Small-scale Hanja notation sits as a superscript label above the dancheong band at the left column boundary, providing categorical anchoring without competing with the statement. Slide number appears alone, bottom-right, at minimal weight — no header band, no rule lines beyond the dancheong strip itself.
